source.title: On the geometry of generalization and memorization in deep neural networks
source.authors: Cory Stephenson; Suchismita Padhy; Abhinav Ganesh; Yue Hui; Hanlin Tang; SueYeon Chung

record.tranche_reason: The study varies model size and measures generalization performance, directly testing model-wise double descent with a different architecture, dataset, and setting.
record.gate_note: The width-scaled ResNet-18 sweep and its test-accuracy results bear on V1. The study also reports a double-descent pattern in manifold dimension, recorded separately as a geometry finding rather than evidence for V5's prediction of peak location. Other memorization, layer-rewinding, gradient, and accuracy-over-training results do not directly test the listed double-descent versions.
record.test_reason: A width-scaled ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 with 10% label noise, following Nakkiran et al., shows test accuracy across model sizes. The authors state that it exhibits double descent (Fig. 4C). This is a close repeat of the original model-wise setting, though a side result of a geometry paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors reproduce model-wise double descent (Fig. 4C) and link it to a double descent in final-epoch object-manifold dimension. Radius and center correlation stay monotonic with size. They propose competing effects of feature dimension as an explanation but leave the mechanism to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a width-scaled ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 with 10% label noise and reports test accuracy, rather than reproducing the original study's complete settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The model-size comparison is reported at both the best epoch and the final epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-epoch test-data object-manifold dimension first decreases, then increases, then decreases with model size. Manifold radius and center correlation are monotonic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-wise double descent in generalization is accompanied by a matching non-monotonic change in class-manifold dimensionality.

record.problems: The model-size results are presented graphically without numerical values in the text. The model-size sweep is one architecture, dataset, and label-noise setting; no control or uncertainty estimate for Figure 4C is stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the model-size double-descent results were left out. Other reported findings were excluded because they do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Whether the peak sits at the interpolation threshold; numerical size of the peak; other architectures or datasets; early-stopped behaviour (cannot be read from the text).
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Only a single noise level (10%); no regularization sweep (no weight decay used).

record.verdict_notes: The record's uncertainty_reported 'y' is not supported for Fig. 4C: no error bars or seed count are stated for the width sweep. The setup closely mirrors Nakkiran et al. (ResNet-18 width, CIFAR-100, 10% noise, Adam lr 1e-4), so this is a near-replication with only qualitative evidence. Training ran up to 1000 epochs or until >99% train accuracy, with no regularization.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests a model-size sweep on ResNet-18; it does not establish the pattern across all deep networks or original settings.
No epoch-wise fall-rise-fall double-descent test is reported.
No training-sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold is reported.
The study does not test double descent across non-deep model classes or broadly across model classes.

The study reports a geometry measure tracking double descent with model size, but does not test whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study does not test whether noise drives the peak, whether descent splits into multiple peaks, or whether tuned regularization removes it.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that produces an ordinary U-shaped curve.
